name: Trick-or-Think: Place Value Regrouping
competency: Understanding 3-digit subtraction across zeros through place-value borrowing, cascading regrouping (Hundreds to Tens to Ones), and value conservation
ncertStandard: Grade 3 Mathematics: Chapter 6 - Fun with Give and Take
overview: Three living place-value houses (Hundreds, Tens, Ones) have 500 candies. When trick-or-treaters need 53 candies, children help Ones borrow from Tens, and Tens borrow from Hundreds. Demonstrates that 1 Hundred = 10 Tens and 1 Ten = 10 Ones, proving that 400 + 90 + 10 = 500 candies before column-by-column subtraction.
learningOutcomes: Understand why you cannot subtract a larger digit from zero
Master the sequential chain of borrowing across neighboring place-value columns
Recognize that 1 Hundred = 10 Tens and 1 Ten = 10 Ones
Verify value conservation: 500 = 400 + 90 + 10 without losing a single unit
